lesson: scripts/roadmap.js, render-sections.js and check-prompt.js run with every CLAUDE_* variable deleted; tests/standalone.test.js spawns them that way, so re-coupling one to the harness fails there first.
check-prompt.js errors are {error, fix, example} objects, not strings; example is always present and null when the fix says enough, and consumers read e.error for the message.

craft-prompt runs one read-only Explore pass before Call 2 and turns it into the file and test-command options; what it returns is a proposal the user Other-answer overrules, and nothing reaches touches unpicked.

The model-side trial events are written by skill prose calling scripts/trial-log.js; an unknown event name or flow validates to nothing and loses the row, so tests/trial_events.test.js checks every name written anywhere in skills/ against the vocabulary.
picks/gen.js backlogs at 10/50/150 all have critical depth 0 or 1 and depth equal to unblocks_total, so every replay strategy returns the same order; use picks/fixtures/deep to separate them.

relevantFilesText in foreman/scripts/craft-handoff.js is the block that decides how much of a touched file a handoff cites; it caps at SYMBOL_KEEP and hoists names the entry prose backticks or writes in camelCase.

foreman no longer asks or dispatches a model: the Agent call omits model, entryParagraphText in scripts/craft-handoff.js always asks the destination to self-report model and effort, and roadmap.js list --stats is the only reader of those two fields.
render-sections.js no longer emits fableEnabled; a config still carrying the key now reports as unknown_config_key from roadmap-doctor.js, a warning and never an error.

checkpointEmbedText in foreman/scripts/craft-handoff.js is baked into the pasted prompt because that session cannot read prompt-template.md — any rule the template states about checkpoint commits must be duplicated into the embed or it never reaches the executing session.

ROADMAP.jsonl's foreman_roadmap_format marker describes the FILE, not each line — an older Foreman can append an old-shaped entry to a stamped file, so any upgrade step in scripts/roadmap.js that is idempotent by shape must run unconditionally rather than on the declared version.

flint output-styles/hush.md is a copy of hush output-styles/hush.md with exactly two removals: the force-for-plugin frontmatter key and the paragraph starting Notes like [hush ...]. Nothing else differs, so a hush style change means re-copying and re-stripping those two.
A new prefixed `notes` line in Foreman must be registered in MACHINE_NOTE_RE in scripts/craft-handoff.js or recallExcerpt will quote it back to a later session as if a human had written it.

prompt-template.md:249 ships verbatim into a reinforced prompt via fullLineContaining(xml, NO_INVENTION_SENTENCE) in craft-handoff.js, so editing that ONE LINE changes what every reinforced handoff says; the standard profile carries CONCISE_TRUTH_SENTENCE from check-prompt.js:96 instead, and the two must be edited together.

buildTaskRows in scripts/craft-handoff.js gives row 1 the whole base prompt and every later row only goal/files/Run/Expected, so a verification pair with no goal and no files splits into a task that contains nothing but a command.

A craft-handoff warning gated on the `tasks` variable only ever fires for destination task; the clipboard embed asks for the same per-check task rows, so any rule about split rows must also test wantsClipboardEmbed.

The Windows clipboard copy command is written in THREE places — prompt-template.md, skills/roadmap/pick.md and skills/craft-prompt/SKILL.md — and no script or test binds them, so any change to it has to be made in all three by hand.

candidateIdentifiers in scripts/resolve-symbols.js runs two regexes and only CALL_SHAPED needed narrowing: COMPOUND_SHAPED already refuses a plain lowercase word, so a bare name like deny only surfaces when the prose backticks it.

buildTaskRows in scripts/craft-handoff.js composes a split row description from pair.goal, pair.subject and pair.files, so any rule about whether a row carries work must read all three - reading only goal and files reports a subject-bearing row as empty.

In scripts/roadmap.js update-status, a trial row about a close must read the entry's status BEFORE `entry.status = status` moves it (the wasClosed const): awaiting_acceptance -> done is a closing status too, so a rule that tests only the new status counts every accepted entry twice.

In scripts/craft-handoff.js a <prior_work> lead's prose comes from leadExcerpt — the entry's why, and recallExcerpt(notes) only when why is empty — and the sort is reach ascending then id DESCENDING; a fixture that puts its distinguishing text in notes, or expects the oldest id first, is asserting the pre-284 behaviour and will read the default why instead.

In scripts/craft-handoff.js every reading of HISTORY (prior-work recall, anchor titles, the ledger overlap trigger) goes through historyEntries, which is readEntries plus readArchive; readEntries alone is only right for the picked entry, because an archived entry cannot be picked — a new consumer that calls readEntries directly silently forgets everything the project archived.

In scripts/craft-handoff.js only priorWorkText applies RECALL_MAX_REACH; selectNotes serves lessons on bare path overlap, newest first then by match count, bounded by NOTES_KEEP and NOTES_MAX_CHARS — a fixture with a single finished entry on the planned path now serves its lesson, where before 286 the 20% rule read that path as too busy.

symbolShapers in scripts/commit-evidence.js runs `git log -L :<name>[^A-Za-z0-9_$]:<file>` in the SUBMODULE scope with the prefix stripped, like changedSince; the trailing bracket class is load-bearing (bare `alpha` also matches `alphaBeta`), git must find the definition line in HEAD (an uncommitted file is null), and null is read by symbolChainText as nothing to say, silently — a chain that fails to appear is usually one of those three.

benchmarks/foreman/benefit/gen.js splices every treatment block at `</relevant_files>\n` in fixtures/pinned-dup/prompts/foreman.md and the runner scores pinned-dup by three sentinels; a chain arm needs only the plugin's CHAIN_HEADER plus one line in the product's `<id> <title> — <why>` shape, and it moved 0/6 to 6/6 on both models, so the chain's format is not what limits it.

A benchmark task can run on another task's fixture with the opposite truth: tasks.json `fixture` plus `solutionDir` (honoured by selfcheck.js) plus `absent: true` sentinels (runner/metrics.js) — and the measured fact is that a false uncheckable lesson flips Sonnet 6/6 to 1/6 while Opus refuses it 6/6 after searching the repo for the ticket, so the ledger's safety rests on the destination model looking, not on the label.

In scripts/craft-handoff.js the four <background> history blocks (prior_work, lessons, symbol chain, anchors) each open with a header framing them as history or as claims to verify against the code; a fact placed in <background> without that frame, or under Constraints:, is obeyed as fact on both models, so never carry an earlier entry's why or a lesson outside those frames.

taskContextText and taskRulesText in scripts/craft-handoff.js relay two entry fields mechanically — why as the 'Why this task exists:' line and planned_touches as the Expected file surface constraint — so a judgment.purpose on an entry handoff is dropped and expectedFileSurface is only an override; any new fact the destination must receive belongs in the script, not in a skill bullet asking the crafter to copy it.

The Pattern: line relevantFilesText adds in scripts/craft-handoff.js rests only on a shared local import (resolve-symbols.js referenceImplementations), so it names that import as its evidence; a hand-written Pattern line keeps the directive form because a user asserted it — keep the two forms distinct rather than unifying them.

promptedNames in scripts/craft-handoff.js is the single ranking signal for relevant_files symbol order AND the symbol chain's candidates, and it reads the record's title, why and what — a symbol named only in a field it does not scan (notes, for instance) is cited in file order or not at all.
